headline: Phillies score seven in eighth, beat Braves 9-4
recap: The Phillies beat the Braves 9-4 in Atlanta on Sunday to close out the series. Atlanta scored first when Drake Baldwin's sacrifice fly brought home Michael Harris II in the first. J.T. Realmuto's two-run homer, his 11th of the season, scored Brandon Marsh and put Philadelphia ahead 2-1 in the second. Matt Olson's RBI single scored Harris II to tie it at 2-2 in the seventh. The Phillies answered with seven runs in the eighth: Alec Bohm's two-run double scored Trea Turner and Bryce Harper, Bryson Stott's single drove in Bohm, J.T. Realmuto's single scored Stott, Kyle Schwarber's two-run single brought home Bryan De La Cruz and Realmuto, and Turner's single scored Justin Crawford to make it 9-2. Matt Olson's two-run homer, his 39th, in the bottom of the ninth scored Ronald Acuña Jr. for the final 9-4 margin. Andrew Painter started and allowed one earned run over five innings; José Alvarado was credited with the win in relief, and Dylan Lee took the loss for Atlanta.
The win snapped a three-game losing streak. The Phillies are 83-67, second in the NL East, five games behind the division-leading Braves.

Philadelphia is off today before opening a two-game series at Washington, with first pitch at Nationals Park scheduled for Tuesday at 6:45 PM ET. Cristopher Sánchez is set to start for the Phillies opposite Jackson Kent for the Nationals.
